It was proclaimed in 1891 and was the first national park in South Australia, second in Australia (after Sydney's Royal National Park which was proclaimed in 1879) and the tenth in the world. The national park lies within the Adelaide Hills and Mitcham council area, and forms part of a chain of protected areas located along the Adelaide Hills Face Zone. The national park is administered by the Department of Environment, Water and Natural Resources.


== Naming ==
For most of its existence, it has been known as the "National Park". Between the years 1972 and 1991 it was known as the "Belair Recreation Park". In 1991, the Belair Recreation Park was abolished and the land that it occupied was constituted as a national park and given the name “Belair National Park”.


== History ==
Belair was originally inhabited by the Kaurna Aboriginal people.
